summary: Built stencilpipe, a standard-library Python 3 library where every operation declares a footprint (the input window it reads for an output window) and a recursive evaluator propagates window requests down a lazy graph, so a small request computes only that window plus each node's reach, clipped at every edge. Every input, sources included, is handed to operations as a guarded Region addressed in absolute coordinates, so a short reach raises FootprintError instead of silently shifting edge values, and whole-grid evaluation runs the same operation code as windowed evaluation so windowed results are bit for bit the cut of the whole result. The hidden global in normalize (the whole-grid maximum) is split into a cached statistic node wired in as an ordinary second input of a local divide, and the suite proves the invariance per operation and in random chains, tests the guard, and checks that the counted work follows the request rather than the grid.

pattern_mapping.Footprint: Operation.footprint(window, index, extent) on each op in stencilpipe/ops.py; WHOLE sentinel in stencilpipe/geometry.py marks a global read
pattern_mapping.Window: plain (x, y, w, h) tuples plus clip_window, grow_window, whole_window in stencilpipe/geometry.py
pattern_mapping.Region evaluator: Engine._eval in stencilpipe/engine.py, called by evaluate / evaluate_many; asks each input for its footprint, clips it, and computes exactly the window
pattern_mapping.Invariance test: tests/test_invariance.py (every op alone, after a blur, before a blur, a deep chain, 25 random chains; exact equality against a cut of the whole result, fresh engine and fresh graph per window)
pattern_mapping.Footprint guard: Region in stencilpipe/geometry.py: rows are trimmed to the footprint and get / slice_row / sum_row raise FootprintError on any read outside it; sources are cut the same way in Engine._eval
pattern_mapping.Global barrier: MaxStat.footprint returning WHOLE in stencilpipe/ops.py; Engine._eval turns it into the input's whole extent, so that input (and only that input) evaluates whole
pattern_mapping.Statistic node: _build_normalize in stencilpipe/engine.py creates MaxStat over the image and wires it as input 1 of Normalize, whose footprint for that one-value input is WHOLE; no evaluator hook is needed
pattern_mapping.Cost rule: not implemented: per-pixel windowed cost is low for these operations, and a whole-run shortcut would make cells_computed and the invariance story harder to reason about
pattern_mapping.Scale conversion: not implemented: TASK.md has a single scale, so reaches are counts of pixels
pattern_mapping.Tile grid / cell memo: not implemented: each requested window is computed on its own (never merged into a bounding box); the only cached whole value is the statistic's exact 1x1 maximum

notes_applied: Note 1 (exact footprint, only a test can say so): test_invariance.py runs every operation alone and in chains, at interior/edge/corner/1x1/whole/overhanging windows, each on a fresh engine and freshly built graph, with r up to 5 and random chains, and asserts exact equality.

Note 2 (arithmetic that ignores the buffer origin): no prefix sums anywhere; sums accumulate row by row and left to right through absolute-coordinate reads, and whole evaluation is literally the same operation code with the whole extent as the window, so windowed and whole results are bit-identical by construction.

Note 3 (guard every read): Region trims rows to the footprint and raises FootprintError from get / slice_row / sum_row; tests/test_guard.py registers a ShortBox (one pixel short reach) and a GreedyAdd (one read outside its window) and expects the error, including when the guarded input is a source.

Note 4 (border rules only at the real border): box clips its square to the input's whole extent (carried on the Region) and counts only existing cells, so windowed evaluation meets the same border a whole run would.
Note 5 (reaches add along a chain): widening happens per node in Engine._eval; test_cost.py asserts the 4x3 window grown by 2+1 reaches 10x9 for dx -> box(1) -> box(2).

Note 7 (find hidden globals and wire the statistic as an input): normalize is split into MaxStat (whole footprint, cached) and Normalize (point footprint for the image, WHOLE for the statistic); test_global.py shows the window uses the whole-grid maximum and differs from dividing by the window's maximum, so two zooms agree on a cell.

Note 8 (no cost rule on the bounding box): no cost rule at all, and evaluate_many evaluates each window separately (test_cost.py checks far-apart windows cost their own cells, not the 200-cell bounding box).

Note 9 (keep the best case, measure cold): the statistic's exact whole value is checked first and reused, cutting any requested window from it; fresh engines in most tests start cold, and one test shows a warmed engine gives the same values as a cold one.
Note 11 (measurements around items are window requests): each entry of evaluate_many is its own request, never their bounding box.
tests: 55 tests in six files plus a support module; last run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 'Ran 55 tests in 0.221s / OK'. A separate one-off fuzz (60 random chains x all probe windows) found 0 mismatches, and a 1200x800 check computed a 64x64 window of box(r=32) in 0.21 s with 4096 counted cells.
chapter_feedback: Helped most: implementation note 7 predicted the normalize trap exactly, and note 1's insistence on a fresh engine per window and on edge/corner/1x1 windows shaped the invariance matrix that gives the design its confidence.

Helped: note 3's demand for a guard on every read, sources included, turned an invisible class of bug into a loud FootprintError; writing the deliberately short-reach test was easy because the guard exists.

Mislead me on cost: the Sketch's cost rule compares sum(area(fp)) with sum(area(input.extent)), i.e. input areas, while TASK.md's cells_computed counts output cells per operation. I first wrote cost tests using footprint areas (expecting 52 and 272 cells instead of 32 and 102) and had to correct my model: a point consumer asks its input for exactly its own window, so a blur's reach is visible in the counter only through a consumer that has a reach.

Mislead me slightly on notes 4 and the Sketch's resize footprint: 'map the window back' is not enough for half(), because whether 2x+1 exists is a fact about the whole input extent, not about the footprint window; the Region has to carry the producing node's extent so the existence test and the clamp in dx() are right at a window's edge.

Left to guess: whether the statistic node's single output cell should be counted by cells_computed. I count it (TASK.md: every operation must count every cell it computes), so one normalize window costs w*h + 1 and later windows w*h; a test expecting exactly w*h would disagree.

Left to guess: normalize when the maximum is 0 and the grid has negative cells (TASK.md only says '0 stays 0 if m is 0'); I divide nothing and return 0.0 for the whole window, which is exact and window-stable.

Left to guess: whether overlapping windows should share work. I chose the chapter's smallest form (no tiles, no cell memo, only the cached statistic), which keeps cells_computed honest but recomputes an overlap twice.
